core.title: Bind every required telemetry item to a test via a telemetry binding
core.given: An acceptance with required telemetry lists a concrete telemetry item identifier that the tracking plan contains (a required item)
core.when: Required items, the tracking plan, or test files' telemetry bindings are added, changed or removed
core.then: Ensure at least one test file binds each required item via its telemetry binding.
prefer: Add a telemetry test whose bindings name both the acceptance and the required telemetry item (binding syntax from the profile), and whose body proves the item is emitted.
avoid: Leaving a required item planned and implemented but untested.
Adding a telemetry binding to a test that does not exercise the item just to close the gap.
unless: Diagnostic logs and internal spans an acceptance does not require need no dedicated test — only required items are covered by this closure.
Inert until the repository adopts this rule family.
core.why: Evidence leg of the traceability tripod (planned, implemented, tested): the coder rule binds the implementation, this binds the proof. A required item no test covers is a plan nobody can rely on.
evidence: For every required item (acceptance-required identifier present in the tracking plan) at least one test file carries a telemetry binding naming it.
The convention check for this rule reports no uncovered required items.
verification: Compute required items as the intersection of acceptance-required telemetry identifiers with tracking-plan items; collect test bindings from every telemetry binding in any test file (no filename pattern or task reference required); the set difference — required items without a binding — is the finding set.
Report each uncovered required item at the tracking-plan item's own file.
A required identifier that cannot be resolved in the tracking plan belongs to the acceptance-decision rule and is not double-reported here.
The check runs only where the repository has adopted this rule family; the rule is inert before adoption.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding (no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).

fires: An acceptance with required telemetry lists an item that exists in the tracking plan, and no test file anywhere carries a telemetry binding naming it.
An acceptance newly requires a tracking-plan item (or the item is added to the plan) and no test binds it.
After a test is deleted or its telemetry binding removed, an adopted, still-required, resolvable item has no remaining test binding.
doesNotFire: A diagnostic log or internal span that no acceptance requires has no dedicated test.
A required item cannot be resolved in the tracking plan (reported by the acceptance-decision rule instead).
A telemetry binding is removed but another test file still binds the same required item.
The repository has not adopted the telemetry rule family.

profileRequirements.meaning: How one telemetry item is identified: the concrete telemetry URN carried by its tracking-plan entry. Acceptance decisions, tracking-plan entries and test bindings all refer to an item by this exact identifier, so the obligation covers every required URN of that form; no narrower grammar is imposed (the single metric URN shown in the fix hint is realization example data only).
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a telemetry item — the telemetry binding this rule's obligation is expressed in.
The syntax by which a test binds itself to the acceptance it proves, named alongside the telemetry binding in the preferred telemetry test.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral: every acceptance-required, plan-resolvable telemetry item must be bound by at least one test's telemetry binding. Two concrete things the core needs have no existing vocabulary key and are proposed: the telemetry item identifier contract (urn.telemetry_item) and its binding syntax (urn.binding.telemetry); urn.binding.acceptance already exists. urn.telemetry_item's Bun value is bun.json's own placeholder <telemetry-urn> — an exact-identifier contract covering every telemetry URN in the tracking plan — since bun.json states no general URN grammar and the fix hint's telemetry:metric:... URN is a single illustrative instance kept only as realization example data (verifier_detail[4], bunOnly). 'Tracking plan' and 'acceptance decision' are treated as role-level plan-artifact kinds (file_kind facts), not paths, so no layout/roots key is required. The activation fact value telemetry_header_removed was renamed telemetry_binding_removed (a header is Bun's binding idiom). The validator id bun_telemetry_test, the shared strict-disposition policy wording, and the project-specific fix hint (file path and concrete URNs) remain bunOnly; severity 2 and strict disposition live in core:verification, not in the profile.
